hypothesis: Lock research design
change: Created protocol and clean-panel scope
motivation: Prevent untracked adaptation before final test
metric: N/A
result: Design locked
decision: Proceed
notes: 2024-2025 is final test only and is not a validation window

hypothesis: Build point-in-time eligible universe
change: Added auditable classification and investability rules plus 20-trading-day target
motivation: Establish a leakage-safe research panel before signals
metric: Panel validation
result: 21104236 panel rows; 8399139 eligible; 8321030 eligible with target
decision: Proceed
notes: 2024-2025 remains final test only; target is censored if 20 later returns are incomplete

hypothesis: Medium-term momentum (skip most recent 20 days) predicts positive 20-day forward cross-sectional returns
change: Added mom_120_20 factor and the reusable single-factor evaluation harness (IC, deciles, rank autocorrelation, coverage, non-overlapping 20-day long-short with turnover and costs)
motivation: First vertical slice of Week 2; establishes the template applied identically to the other five signals
metric: Mean Spearman IC; Newey-West(20) t-stat; gross/net Sharpe at 1/5/10/20 bps
result: Mean rank IC -0.00002 (NW t=-0.00); mean Pearson IC 0.0056 (NW t=0.73); decile returns non-monotonic (hump peaking at D3); rank autocorr 0.987 (1d) / 0.768 (20d); turnover 0.895 per rebalance; gross Sharpe 0.188; net Sharpe 0.178/0.138/0.088/-0.011 at 1/5/10/20bp; breakeven ~19bp; -41.6% worst period in the 2009 momentum crash
decision: Keep in the six-signal set as a documented null; do not re-tune the window; do not treat as a standalone strategy
notes: 2024-2025 sealed: last evaluated date 2023-11-30 so no target window reaches into 2024. Memo: reports/factor_memo_01_momentum.md

hypothesis: Recent five-day losers outperform over the next 20 days
change: Added rev_5 = -sum of the last five daily returns
motivation: Plan 5.2 short-term reversal
metric: Mean Spearman IC; NW(20) t; gross/net Sharpe
result: Rank IC +0.0077 (t=2.12); deciles rise monotonically D1-D9 then D10 collapses; turnover 1.74; gross Sharpe 0.149; breakeven 6.0bp; net Sharpe -0.108 at 10bp
decision: Keep with caution: does not survive Bonferroni across the six tests, and offset spread is -0.32 to +0.55
notes: Long-short book longs D10, the one decile that breaks the pattern

hypothesis: High realized volatility predicts lower 20-day returns
change: Added rvol_20 = sqrt(sum of squared returns over t-20..t-1)
motivation: Plan 5.3 realized volatility
metric: Mean Spearman IC; NW(20) t; gross/net Sharpe
result: Signed rank IC +0.0286 (t=-2.85 raw, correct direction); effect is concentrated in D10 at 0.45% vs 0.94% interior peak; turnover 1.22; gross Sharpe 0.161; breakeven 14.0bp; net Sharpe 0.047 at 10bp
decision: Keep as the strongest single candidate; survives Bonferroni
notes: D1 is below the interior peak, so this is a short of high volatility rather than a low-volatility premium

hypothesis: Abnormally high volume predicts higher 20-day returns
change: Added vs_20 = log(turnover_t / mean turnover over t-20..t-1)
motivation: Plan 5.4 volume surprise
metric: Mean Spearman IC; NW(20) t; gross/net Sharpe
result: Rank IC +0.0056 (t=3.43, most significant of the six); gross Sharpe 0.344; turnover 1.84; breakeven 5.6bp; net Sharpe -0.273 at 10bp
decision: Keep, but record that it is statistically real and economically unusable on its own
notes: Turnover rather than share volume, because price/volume/shares are as-traded in this export and a split cancels out of the turnover ratio

hypothesis: Momentum in market-model residuals predicts higher 20-day returns
change: Added rmom_120_20: OLS on 252 days ending t-21, residuals summed over t-120..t-21 in closed form
motivation: Plan 5.5 residual momentum
metric: Mean Spearman IC; NW(20) t; gross/net Sharpe
result: Rank IC -0.0036 (t=-0.63), wrong sign, negative in 12 of 18 years; gross Sharpe 0.059; breakeven 3.7bp; coverage 98.98% with 20 zero-coverage dates in Jan 2006 because the factor needs 273 days of history
decision: Keep only for the Week 5 ablation
notes: Residualising did not rescue momentum; it removed what little was left

hypothesis: Stocks near their 252-day high outperform stocks in deep drawdown
change: Added dd_252 on the cumulative total-return index, not on price
motivation: Plan 5.6 drawdown
metric: Mean Spearman IC; NW(20) t; gross/net Sharpe
result: Rank IC +0.0150 (t=1.39, insignificant); hump-shaped deciles, D1 0.60% and D10 0.67% against an interior peak of 0.98%; turnover 1.00; gross Sharpe 0.032; breakeven 3.6bp
decision: Keep as a control
notes: Measured on returns because price is not split-adjusted in this export

hypothesis: Portfolio statistics are sensitive to the rebalance offset and to the drawdown convention
change: Averaged all 20 rebalance offsets instead of one; floored the drawdown peak at starting wealth 1.0
motivation: A single-offset book gave rev_5 a negative gross Sharpe despite a significantly positive IC
metric: Gross Sharpe mean and spread across the 20 offsets
result: Offset spread is widest for the high-turnover factors: rev_5 -0.315 to +0.547, vs_20 0.065 to 0.630. Momentum gross Sharpe 0.188 -> 0.147 and breakeven ~19bp -> ~14.9bp
decision: Adopt offset averaging as the standard convention; supersede the portfolio numbers in W2-001
notes: Estimator change only; no factor was re-tuned and 2024-2025 remains sealed

hypothesis: Volume surprise and drawdown require same-close execution unless their inputs are lagged one day
change: Lagged vs_20 to turnover at t-1 against t-21..t-2, and dd_252 to the drawdown at t-1 against the peak over t-252..t-1; strengthened the shared leakage test to perturb row t itself
motivation: The target runs from the close of t, so a signal needing t's own close could only be executed at the instant the return starts accruing
metric: Mean Spearman IC; NW(20) t; gross Sharpe; breakeven cost
result: vs_20 signed IC 0.0056->0.0039, NW t 3.43->2.50, gross Sharpe 0.344->0.256, breakeven 5.6bp->4.1bp, no longer survives Bonferroni across six tests. dd_252 nearly unchanged: t 1.39->1.44, gross Sharpe 0.032->0.044
decision: Adopt the lagged definitions; all six factors are now determined by the close of t-1
notes: About a third of the volume-surprise IC was an execution assumption. rvol_20 is now the only factor surviving the multiple-testing correction.

hypothesis: The six factors are not six independent bets
change: Built the aligned six-factor rank panel and measured cross-sectional rank and daily portfolio-return correlations
motivation: Week 2 decile shapes suggested momentum, volatility, drawdown and residual momentum share one distressed/high-volatility exposure
metric: Mean daily rank correlation; daily gross portfolio-return correlation
result: rmom vs mom: rank 0.73, returns 0.76. rvol vs dd: rank -0.48 but returns +0.87. mom vs dd returns 0.75. Only rev_5 and vs_20 are distinct; vs_20's book has no return correlation above 0.17
decision: Treat the four as one cluster; let Week 4 models set weights rather than assuming an equal composite
notes: Return correlation is the informative measure: mom and rvol look independent by rank (-0.10) but their books correlate 0.46

hypothesis: Walk-forward folds must be purged by the target horizon
change: Added ten fixed expanding-window folds with a 20-trading-day purge before each validation year
motivation: An observation at t carries a target to t+20, so training to the boundary trains on validation-year returns
metric: Fold structure; purge length
result: Ten folds, train 1973 to 4239 days, exactly 20 trading days purged in every fold, final validation stops 2023-11-30
decision: Fix these splits for Weeks 4-5
notes: No fold can reach the sealed period

hypothesis: A dollar-neutral rank-weighted book is a usable baseline
change: Built the capped, dollar-neutral, 20-day staggered-cohort portfolio with daily P&L, turnover, costs and exposures
motivation: Week 2's single-offset rebalance was an unstable estimator; staggered cohorts use every start date at once
metric: Gross/net Sharpe; turnover; breakeven; market beta
result: Composite gross Sharpe 0.121, breakeven 8.7bp, net -0.018 at 10bp. Nothing clears 10bp. Position cap never binds (largest position 0.35% vs 1% cap). Fast signals self-cancel across cohorts: gross exposure 0.39-0.44 for vs_20 and rev_5
decision: Adopt as the Week 4 baseline
notes: Dollar-neutral is not beta-neutral: rvol beta -0.34, dd -0.28, composite -0.23, negative in every rolling window

hypothesis: Rank-continuous weights capture more of these signals than tail deciles
change: Ran both weightings through the identical staggered-cohort estimator so the comparison isolates the weighting
motivation: Week 2 argued rank weights should help because five of six factors have hump-shaped deciles
metric: Gross Sharpe and turnover under each weighting
result: REJECTED. Decile weighting wins 5 of 7 on gross Sharpe and 6 of 7 on turnover. Best net book overall is the decile composite: Sharpe 0.001 at 10bp and 10.1bp breakeven, vs -0.018 and 8.7bp for rank
decision: Keep rank weighting as the pre-declared Week 4 baseline anyway, and carry both forward
notes: The Week 2 mechanism was right but the conclusion backwards: rank weights do not avoid the broken tail buckets, they add the low-signal middle 80% and its turnover. Switching the baseline after seeing the winner would be the degrees-of-freedom problem the protocol prevents.

hypothesis: A model fitted on the six factor ranks forecasts the 20-day cross-sectional return better than an equal-weighted composite
change: Added src/models/walk_forward.py: OLS, Ridge and HistGradientBoosting fitted independently in each of the ten folds
motivation: Week 3 showed the composite loads mostly on one correlated cluster; a fitted model can reweight toward the independent signals
training_window: Expanding, 2006-02-01 to each fold train_end (3.0M to 6.9M rows)
validation_window: Ten fixed folds, 2014-2023, 4293065 scored rows per model
metric: Out-of-sample R2, Pearson IC, rank IC with Newey-West t at 20 lags
result: OOS R2 negative for all three (-0.00065 ols, -0.00065 ridge, -0.00042 gbm); rank IC 0.0220 ols (t 8.82), 0.0221 ridge (t 8.59), 0.0197 gbm (t 7.74)
decision: Keep
notes: No point-prediction skill; the entire edge is in cross-sectional ordering. gbm has the highest Pearson IC and the lowest rank IC. LightGBM not installed; sklearn histogram booster used instead

hypothesis: Model-driven books beat the pre-registered composite net of costs
change: Fed each model's predictions through the unchanged Week 3 staggered-cohort backtest under rank and decile weighting
motivation: A significant IC does not imply a tradable book; Week 2 already found one case where it did not
validation_window: Ten folds concatenated into one continuous 2014-2023 daily series, 2496 days
metric: Gross and net Sharpe at 1/5/10/20 bp, breakeven bp, turnover, beta, max drawdown
result: Composite gross Sharpe 0.333 and breakeven 25.0 bp beats every model; best model gbm__decile 0.174 and 10.5 bp; ols and ridge net-negative at 10 bp
decision: Reject the models
notes: Null result. Models trade more for less: ols earns 0.74% gross on a 0.70 book at 6.8x turnover against the composite's 2.81% on a 0.90 book at 5.6x

hypothesis: The Week 3 headline is a valid comparison bar for Week 4
change: Recomputed the composite through identical per-fold machinery restricted to the 2014-2023 validation dates
motivation: Comparing a 2014-2023 model against a 2006-2023 baseline would be a window artefact, not a result
training_window: None; the composite is not fitted
metric: Gross Sharpe and breakeven bp on matched dates, plus t-statistics on sub-period difference
result: Composite gross Sharpe 0.121 over 2006-2023 becomes 0.333 over 2014-2023; breakeven 8.7 bp becomes 25.0 bp; reproduces the Week 3 daily series to 1e-16
decision: Replace the bar
notes: The 0.147 / 10.1 bp target in PROGRESS.md was stale. Sub-period Sharpe difference is +0.441 with SE 0.477 (t 0.92): no evidence the decades differ. Every book in the study has |t| <= 1.06 against zero

hypothesis: Inner-validation MSE identifies the Ridge penalty
change: Probed the alpha grid beyond its pre-registered upper bound and measured the effect on the cross-sectional ordering
motivation: The search returned the grid maximum in all ten folds, which means the grid, not the data, chose the value
metric: Inner MSE across alpha, and mean daily cross-sectional Spearman correlation between prediction sets
result: MSE falls monotonically out to alpha 1e10 for a total 0.005% improvement; predictions at alpha 1e4 and 1e10 correlate only 0.86 by daily rank
decision: Keep the pre-registered grid, change the criterion in Week 5
notes: MSE cannot identify the alpha yet the alpha materially changes the portfolio: ridge rotates coefficients rather than scaling them, so momentum's loading flips sign. Not retuned after the fact, by protocol

hypothesis: The 20-day warm-up block used to pre-ramp each fold's book is safe
change: Removed the warm-up: predictions and cohorts are validation-only, and the ten folds run as one continuous 2014-2023 backtest with cohorts carrying across annual model changes
motivation: A model fit through train_end has already seen the returns realised during train_end+1..train_end+20, which is exactly the warm-up window, so cohorts formed there trade on look-ahead
training_window: Unchanged, expanding to each fold train_end
validation_window: 2014-01-03 to 2023-12-29, one continuous 2515-day series, all eight books on an identical date index
metric: Gross Sharpe before and after removing the warm-up
result: Model books fell 31-43% of gross Sharpe (gbm__decile 0.174 to 0.099); composite fell 11% (0.333 to 0.297), which is the ramp window and year-end tails alone since it depends on no fitted model
decision: Correct and recompute
notes: Withdrew the first version's portfolio numbers. Prediction IC/R2 unaffected: scored rows were never in the warm-up. Also fixed an unintended per-fold cohort reset that truncated year-end tail P&L. Composite reproduces the Week 3 daily series exactly except the 19 ramp days. Regression test added

hypothesis: Sharpe x sqrt(years) is adequate inference for these books
change: Replaced portfolio t-statistics with Newey-West HAC at 20 lags on mean daily gross return, reporting both
motivation: 20 staggered daily cohorts induce serial dependence in the daily series, so the naive statistic overstates precision
metric: HAC t-statistic at 20 lags versus naive Sharpe x sqrt(years)
result: Composite HAC t 1.01 (naive 0.94); every model book 0.26-0.32; the two statistics agree to within 0.07 everywhere
decision: Adopt HAC
notes: The correction is mild here but the verdict is unchanged and now defensible: no book in the study, baseline included, is distinguishable from zero. Ridge deliberately not retuned; rank-IC selection deferred to Week 5 as a declared training-only robustness experiment
